note: The only table translating structured specs/conformance/calculator-cases.json inputs into `noble calculator` stdin lines. Expected values and categories always come from the cases file; this table never adds an expected span or value the case does not state, except the explicitly derived follow-up probes for CALC-07 `rejected_definition_installed: false`.

spelling.source: README.md, Experimental calculator: `let NAME = EXPR` or `fn NAME(P, ...)=EXPR`

define-variable-success-source: crates/noble-cli/src/calculator.rs: a `let` line formats its value before committing State and returns Outcome::Value, so the CLI prints it; a successful `fn` returns Outcome::Defined and prints nothing
echo-expectation: the printed value equals the expression when the expression is a canonical integer literal; otherwise any exact display line matches (the cases file states no value for a definition)

display.source: README.md: results print as `n/d`, or `n` when the denominator is 1
display.default: numerator when denominator is "1", else numerator/denominator

CALC-01.expect: value: display(vector.numerator, vector.denominator) in default mode

CALC-03.expect: diagnostic: vector.category (the case states no span; the observed span is recorded only)

CALC-06.input: all operations, rendered with `spelling`, form one session (one process, one stdin)
CALC-06.expect: define-variable without expected_error: echo; define-function without expected_error: silent; expected_fraction: value in default display; expected_error: diagnostic category only

CALC-09.input: vector.fraction (`n/d`) is one stdin line evaluated as an exact division

CALC-09-later-features.note: CALC-09's `later_features` are outside the Calculator-v1 line grammar and must be refused explicitly (`exact-display-or-explicit-unsupported-feature`, `silent_approximation: false`, `truncated_decimal_labeled_exact: false`). Each probe's category follows from the grammar: an out-of-grammar construct reaches name resolution or trailing input, and a fractional power reaches the numeric domain. No probe's span is stated, so the runner compares the category only.
CALC-09-later-features.reading: The probes meet `explicit-unsupported-feature` only under the derived reading "refused under any named category, never approximated". That reading is not registered by the case and needs an explicit owner or reviewer acceptance, or a case wording amendment, before CALC-09 is promoted.
CALC-09-later-features.caveat: The categories are generic grammar and name categories, so an unsupported feature is indistinguishable from a typo: `sin(1)` reports the same `UnknownName [0,3)` as `sni(1)`, `1 m` reports the same `TrailingInput` as `1 2`, and a user definition `fn sin(x) = x` makes `sin(1)` evaluate. The shell's `Unsupported` category is an internal pending/stage-failure fallback with a zero span, not a feature refusal, so the probes are never mapped to it. These vectors therefore observe explicit refusal and the absence of silent approximation, not a distinct unsupported-feature category.
CALC-09-later-features.derived_from: specs/conformance/calculator-cases.json CALC-09 `input.later_features` and `expected.outcome`; .cairn/specs/calculator/spec.md CALC-PARSE-02 ('Builtin scientific functions are not implicitly available names')

approximation.reason: `^` refuses a non-integer exponent; it never approximates a root.

symbolic-expressions.reason: An unbound identifier reaches name resolution; no symbolic form exists.

trigonometry.reason: A scientific function is not an implicitly available name.

units.reason: The unit identifier after a complete expression is trailing input; the grammar has no unit suffix.

real-arithmetic.reason: An irrational root has no name; values stay exact rationals.

complex-arithmetic.reason: `2i` is a decimal followed by an identifier, so the imaginary suffix is trailing input.

cyclic-imported-definition-graph.reason: The calculator line grammar has no import or module syntax, so an imported definition graph has no CLI spelling.

resource-capability-capture.reason: The calculator line grammar names no resources or capabilities, so a capture has no CLI spelling.

CALC-07-outcomes.otherwise: diagnostic with that category; the case states no span, so the observed span is recorded only
